name: Mahasamghika-Lokottaravada (position-entry)
evidence_basis: An extensive Indic-language textual witness with a lineage colophon, interpreted alongside comparative Vinaya and Buddhist-school evidence.
own_corpus_survival: The Mahavastu survives extensively in Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit; the wider school corpus is only partially preserved.
dates_notes: This entry marks a Mahasamghika branch attested by the Mahavastu and its transmission history. The dates concern the surviving textual and institutional horizon, not the disputed chronology of early Buddhist schisms or a settled date for the school’s separation.
core_thesis: Mahasamghika-Lokottaravada names an early Buddhist lineage represented above all by the Mahavastu. Its transmitted literature gives unusual prominence to the Buddha’s lokottara, or supramundane, character and preserves extensive narratives of former lives, the bodhisattva path, and the Buddha’s career. The Mahavastu is not a concise philosophical treatise, so the tradition should not be reduced to a single doctrine; it is a major source for an early Buddhist understanding of Buddhahood and religious practice outside the lineages represented by the Pali canon. The familiar story that a single figure named Mahadeva caused the school’s division is not sufficiently secure to serve as this entry’s historical basis.

engaged_works.title: Mahavastu
engaged_works.composition_dates_notes: The work is composite and was developed over time; the range is a textual horizon rather than a single date of composition.
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Anonymous and composite. Its colophon associates it with the Lokottaravadin branch of the Mahasamghika, but the work should not be treated as the product of one author.

ascription_evidence.description: The transmitted work identifies its Lokottaravadin Mahasamghika affiliation.

engaged_works.summary: An extensive Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit narrative and disciplinary compilation. It preserves biographies, former-life narratives, accounts of the bodhisattva career, and materials connected with monastic discipline. Its association with the Lokottaravadin Mahasamghika makes it the principal surviving Indic-language anchor for this entry, while its composite form limits claims about a single, uniform doctrinal system.

reception_notes: The Mahavastu is central to modern reconstruction because it preserves a substantial Indic-language witness for a lineage otherwise known through fragmentary, translated, and comparative sources. It should be read as a composite tradition-text, not as transparent evidence for every claim later made about Mahasamghika doctrine.
